messages:
incident-bot: Paging @oncall: Elevated tail latency observed for hosted text-generation. SLO p99 > 2s for last 5m, incident severity: SEV2

enna: I mean emma: grabbing this. seeing alerts in the console — p95 trending up too. starting investigation.

dave: I'm on logs/metrics already. KV cache eviction rate spiked 10x around 13:02 UTC, prefill queues flooding.

maria: streaming stalls reported by customers, one support ticket from alpha-corp mentioning partial responses and hang at 1.5s+ tokens.

cheng: attaching quick metrics snapshot: 
```
kv_cache.items: 1.2M
kv_cache.capacity: 1.6M
kv_cache.evictions_5m: 12480
kv_cache.prefill_rate_1m: 180/s
kv_cache.decode_rate_1m: 55/s
model_streaming.stalls_5m: 320
p95_latency_5m: 780ms -> 1900ms
p99_latency_5m: 1.4s -> 3.8s
cpu_gpu_util_avg: 63% / 88%
```

emma: hypothesis: prefill subsystem is pushing too many entries into KV cache (high prefill_rate) while decode is slower, causing fragmentation and bulk evictions -> tail latency for requests that miss and require repopulation.

alex: agree. this matches previous kv-prefill-eviction patterns. if prefill > decode, we thrash. Need to reduce prefill aggressiveness or increase cache capacity temporarily.

sre-bot: Note: autoscaler cannot add GPUs fast enough for immediate relief due to provisioning delay. fallback option: route traffic to dedicated pool or fall back to smaller model variant.

emma: immediate mitigations I can do: 1) throttle prefill worker concurrency, 2) increase eviction grace TTL for prefills, 3) enable per-tenant fallback to small-model for high-latency requests. I'll try 1+2 now.

dave: how to throttle? is there a flag?

emma: yes, updating runtime config: 
```
PATCH /runtime/config
{
  "prefill": { "max_concurrency": 12, "backoff_ms": 250 }
}
```

maria: also recommend disabling streaming for affected routes temporarily to avoid client-visible partials while we stabilize. customers prefer slower full responses to streaming stalls.

emma: disabling streaming for default route now. running command: 
```
redwoodctl routes update default --streaming=false
```

cheng: i'm pushing a quick config change to increase KV soft limit by 20% on hosted pool to reduce immediate evictions: 
```
kubectl patch configmap kv-cache --patch '{"data":{"soft_capacity":"1920000"}}'
```

sre-bot: change applied to config; rolling update will take ~40s to propagate per node.

alex: i'll open a traffic reroute to dedicated pool for heavy tenants (alpha-corp) to limit impact while we stabilize.

maria: notify support and include suggested mitigation for alpha-corp: switch to non-streaming and retry policy. Drafting message.

emma: update: prefill concurrency lowered, backoff added. evictions rate taking a downward slope. p95 dropping from ~1.9s to ~1.2s after 90s. p99 still high but trending.

dave: logs show a small subset of requests generating huge prefill loads (long context + many function calls). We should patch path that triggers excessive prefill to use lazy prefill.

emma: Agree. I'll add a temporary rule to skip prefill for requests with ctx_tokens > 8k. Command: 
```
redwoodctl policy add skip-prefill --if "ctx_tokens > 8000"
```

cheng: customer alpha-corp now on fallback pool; metrics look better for them. Good call.

maria: support updated alpha-corp: "We've applied a temporary routing change and turned off streaming while we mitigate. Expect improved latency in ~2 minutes."

emma: further action items: 
- short-term: keep throttled prefill and increased soft_capacity for 30m
- mid-term: revisit prefill heuristics and implement prefill-to-decode pacing (rate limiter that uses decode throughput)
- long-term: smarter KV placement and adaptive eviction based on hit-value

alex: I'll take the mid-term owner. cheng, can you own soft_capacity/ops follow-up?

cheng: yep will run a deeper sample and open an infra PR for adaptive limits.

dave: question for handoff: are there client-facing incidents created? we should mark status page if p99 persists > 5m.

maria: I created an incident page and set status: degraded_performance. Support is triaging incoming tickets and tagging affected customers.

emma: p99 now at ~1.1s and falling. streaming stalls down 70%. evictions 5m down to 2k. Good stabilization.

dave: leaving notes in pager duty for oncall follow-up. I'm stepping off in 30m; emma, can you take handoff?

emma: taking handoff. summary for next oncall: initial cause = prefill > decode imbalance causing KV cache fragmentation and high eviction storms; mitigations applied = prefill throttling, soft_capacity bump, disable streaming for default route, targeted routing to dedicated pool for heavy tenants. Continue monitoring p95/p99, evictions, prefill_rate vs decode_rate.

maria: tagging logs + query pointers: 
- kql: `kv_cache.evictions_5m > 1000`
- trace set: `trace:request.prefill_path`

sre-bot: Reminder: create follow-up ticket with RCA and remediation timeline.

emma: will create RCA doc and assign owners: alex (prefill heuristics), cheng (cache limits/ops), dave (alert tuning), maria (customer comms).

alex: thanks. I'll start a draft PR for prefill-to-decode pacing and a canary for the change.

emma: final note before I close this thread: if you see p99 climb again, escalate to SEV1 and consider temporary capacity scale + broader model fallback. Otherwise I'll monitor for the next 2 hours then update RCA. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident closed for now (mitigated) — reopen if metrics breach thresholds again.
